teams.name: Papas McButt Nuggets

nameHistory.name: Why dont you just call them?

teams.commentary: The McButt Nuggets are 3-0, first for the second straight week, and the most convincing thing about them is how many mistakes they can absorb. Jordan picked up Justin Herbert on Thursday, the same Herbert that Frum had just cut, and started him for 12.7 while Bo Nix scored 24.1 on the bench. He won by 33.6 anyway, because Jaxon Smith-Njigba went for 30.2 and has now returned 90.4 points on an $18 keeper. Jeremiyah Love, flagged as his worst pick on draft day at $43, scored 19.4 and is doing his best to get that grade overturned. The easiest remaining schedule in the league is still ahead, which is the scariest sentence in this whole write-up.

teams.name: Christopher Dootron
teams.commentary: Christopher Dootron is 3-0 and up to second, and the secret is simple: nobody scores on Sam. His opponents have totaled 221.7 points, the fewest in the league, and the luck column thanks them for their service. The best move of the week was his: Tyler Shough, picked up Wednesday, started, 23.8. His worst decision was a familiar one, for the third straight week: the Chiefs defense scored 7, second-best among all starting defenses, and was still the worst of his three, because the Vikings scored 19 and the Raiders 11 on the bench. The roster now runs as long as Carly Rae Jepsen's new 24-track double album, and Bijan's 34.3 covers a lot of filler. The real problem is the backfield: Jordan Mason is on IR, so there is literally nobody behind Bijan and Omarion Hampton, who scored 5.6 as the $59 pick flagged as the worst of his draft. One tweaked hamstring and Sam is starting a waiver-wire running back for a 3-0 team.

teams.name: Cachasol Cartel

nameHistory.name: C u M C back KIDZ!!!

teams.commentary: The draft favorite finally showed up. The Cartel posted 141.4, the top score of the week, beat every team in the all-play and handed Frum a 55-point loss, and the committee moves Mike D. up two spots to third. Dak Prescott started for 18.9, Juwan Johnson went from bench bomb in Week 1 to a 19.3 starter, and the Texans defense that scored -4 for him in Week 1 posted the best defensive number in the league on a day Houston lost to fall to 0-3. The only leftovers were Terry McLaurin's 16.7 on the bench. Behind Derrick Henry and Javonte Williams sits Cam Skattebo, a bench back projected at 10.7 points a game, and McLaurin is a spare receiver, which makes Mike D. the most important phone number in a league that's running out of running backs.

teams.name: $200 Dolla Holla
teams.commentary: The Dolla Holla has scored the most points in the league and owns the best all-play record at 25-8, so the move up two spots to fourth is overdue. ESPN's overreaction column is asking whether Brock Purdy is the MVP front-runner, and Hearn, who benched him in Week 2, has come around: Purdy started and delivered 31.2, and George Kittle added 23.2. Then there is the defense. Hearn started the Packers, his own Week 2 pickup, and got -6, while the Jaguars scored 13 on his bench; the Packers have now produced one point on his roster in two weeks. A.J. Brown and Alec Pierce are both on IR and the receiver room still goes Watson, Egbuka, Malik Washington, Josh Downs and Deebo Samuel, so Hearn can afford to move one, and D'Andre Swift is a spare running back on top of that.

teams.name: DINO NUGGETS

nameHistory.name: The Man the Myth the Legend

teams.commentary: Jahmyr Gibbs scored three touchdowns and 37.9 fantasy points, and the Dino Nuggets rode him up two spots to fifth with a 20-point win over Danny. Harold Fannin Jr., who sat on the bench last week, started and scored 20.6, so the lineup card is learning. It isn't finished learning: Jakobi Meyers scored 15.9 on the bench while Xavier Worthy scored 3, and Justin Jefferson, flagged as his worst pick on draft day at $51, managed 4.2. Seattle's 12-game win streak ended against Marcus Mariota, and Baker's Seahawks defense chipped in 4. Three weeks in, Baker has made zero roster moves, and with Rico Dowdle carrying an OUT tag there is nobody healthy behind Gibbs and Chuba Hubbard at running back. That's not a depth chart, it's a prayer, and a manager with five receivers should be shopping one of them for a back.

teams.name: Captain Casper's Low Risk Tacos

nameHistory.name: Coach Matty Ps D In Swishs V

teams.commentary: The Tacos won with the eighth-best score of the week, 88.7 to 86.9, and slide two spots to sixth because the committee watched the tape. De'Von Achane was the bust of the week at 1.7 and is now on injured reserve, while Aaron Jones scored 11.7 on the bench. Jordan Love, a Thursday pickup, scored 18.4 on the bench while Josh Allen played through a questionable tag for 16.8 in a game the Bills won despite five turnovers. Taylor Swift became the most-awarded artist in VMA history on Sunday, and her husband is now outscoring Brett's two starting running backs combined. The good news is the backfield: with Achane on IR, Jaylen Warren, Jones and RJ Harvey are all still behind Saquon, one of the deepest running back rooms in the league, and Michael Pittman Jr. and Brian Thomas Jr. back up the receivers.

teams.name: Table Shepherds McPie

nameHistory.name: your son rip  on line toot
Fernet and The Music Hall Mack

teams.commentary: Foy drops five spots to seventh, the biggest fall on the board, and he did it to himself. He picked up the Giants defense on Sunday, left it on the bench, and watched it score 9 in a 12-7 win in the rain while the Eagles, the top-projected defense of the week, scored -1 in his lineup. Wan'Dale Robinson scored 15.2 on the bench too, and either swap wins a game he lost by 1.8. The kicker situation was addressed as requested: he cut Harrison Mevis after a 3-point week, picked up Daniel Carlson, and got 3. Foy has the hardest remaining schedule in the league, starting with Jordan. He also has six receivers behind Amon-Ra and nothing behind Kyren Williams and David Montgomery projected above seven points a game, so a receiver-for-back swap is sitting right there.

teams.name: For Heaven Sakes, Woman
teams.commentary: Avengers: Endgame won the weekend box office seven years after its release, and Hess ran the same play: Stafford, McCaffrey and Davante Adams combined for 57.7 points. The rest of the cast didn't show. Hess picked up Kenyon Sadiq in Week 2 and kept him on the bench, where he scored 20 while Jalen Coker scored 2.8 in the flex, a 17.2-point swing that looks worse every time you read it. Puka Nacua and Jayden Reed both sit on the bench with OUT tags, and the backups behind them, Tre Tucker at receiver and Kaleb Johnson at running back, both project under six points a game. Hess needs a trade at two positions and has nothing spare to offer, which is the hard part.

teams.name: Ammonia Coladas
teams.commentary: The Coladas had the best lineup efficiency in the league at 92.2% and still posted the lowest score of the week, 78.2, which means the roster is the problem. The Patriots defense scored 0 in a 35-6 loss to Jacksonville, and Drake Maye, who now leads the NFL with seven turnovers, was at least correctly left on the bench. Mark once called his team Scrubs City, and the name has migrated to his bench: five running backs, and Brian Robinson Jr. (11) and George Holani (8.3) both outscored starter Kyle Monangai (3.1). Nico Collins is parked on IR, which pushes Mike Evans into the second receiver job with nobody behind him, and with Josh Jacobs also on IR, eight running backs turn out to be one real one plus Kenny Gainwell. Quantity is not depth.

teams.name: Los Desperados Sudados
teams.commentary: Los Desperados are 0-3 with a winning all-play record and the worst luck number in the league, and they've allowed 372.6 points, second-most. This week, though, Danny helped. He picked up the Bengals defense on Wednesday and started it in a Steelers-Bengals shootout for 0, while the Broncos defense, flagged as his worst pick on draft day, scored 9 on the bench. He also cut Baker Mayfield, the quarterback he dropped Jordan Love for last week; Love scored 18.4 this week on Brett A.'s bench. Travis Etienne now carries an OUT tag after 8 points in the flex, Isiah Pacheco is on IR, and the next man up is Rachaad White at 4.9 projected points a game, so Danny needs a running back more than anyone in the league.

teams.name: Quintosss... Amigo?
teams.commentary: Brock Bowers came back with 22.6 and Drake London added 23.9, and the Amigos still lost to Sam by 19.4, which is how you get to 0-3. For the second straight week Patrick Mahomes outscored Jalen Hurts from the bench, 15.9 to 12.5, and Tony Pollard's 11.6 sat behind Tetairoa McMillan's 2.7 in the flex. Breece Hall, flagged as his worst pick on draft day, played through a questionable tag for 7. A manager who once named his team IllSellMySoul ForAWin is 0-3 and apparently hasn't found a buyer. The silver lining is the skill positions: Tony Pollard is a spare back and McMillan and Khalil Shakir are spare receivers, so the 0-3 team is one of the best-stocked sellers in the league.

The Best Butt of the Bunch

teams.commentary: Frum is last again after a 55-point loss, with the league's worst all-play record at 7-26 and the most points allowed. The receipt of the week is the flex: Jadarian Price scored 0.7 there, and every one of the six players on the bench outscored him. Bryce Young finally got the start and scored 13.6, while Justin Herbert, whom he cut this week, scored 12.7 for Jordan, so that one's a wash. Dalton Schultz, also picked up Wednesday, started at tight end and scored 4.5 while Colston Loveland scored 5.1 on the bench. Frum once named his team Lots of ??? But Tons of Upside!, and the receivers have nailed the first half: behind Zay Flowers and Jaylen Waddle it's Dontayvion Wicks at 5.8 projected points a game. With Charbonnet on IR he still has Tuten, Price and Woody Marks at running back, so he has backs to sell and every reason to sell one.

commentary.author: Claude
commentary.intro: Seattle's 12-game win streak died to Marcus Mariota, Houston fell to 0-3 for the second year running, and Fadunkadunk had the same kind of Sunday: the favorites finally looked like favorites and a couple of contenders tripped over their own benches. Mike D.'s Cartel, the A-plus draft favorite, posted the week's top score, went 11-0 in the all-play and buried Frum by 55. Jordan stays on top at 3-0 with the softest schedule left in the league. Sam also sits at 3-0 and climbs to second, having allowed 221.7 points, more than 50 fewer than anyone else, which is less a defense than a scheduling miracle. The fall of the week belongs to Foy, who drops five spots after losing by 1.8 with the game-winner sitting on his bench. At the bottom, Danny, Jeff and Frum are all 0-3, and only Danny has a winning all-play record to blame on the schedule.

awards.benchBomb: Hearn started the Packers defense (-6) and benched the Jaguars (13), who spent Sunday turning Drake Maye's turnovers into a 35-6 rout. He won by 43.6, so the only casualty was his dignity.
awards.closest: Brett A. over Foy, 88.7 to 86.9. Foy had the Giants defense (9) and Wan'Dale Robinson (15.2) on his bench, and either one wins it.
awards.blowout: Mike D. over Frum by 55: the best score of the week against the second-worst.
awards.highScore: Cachasol Cartel, 141.4, with an 11-0 all-play. The A-plus draft grade has entered the chat.
awards.lowScore: Ammonia Coladas, 78.2, and no all-play wins. The lineup was right. The roster wasn't.
awards.worstDefense: Hearn's Packers, a Week 2 pickup, finished at -6 and have now scored one point on his roster.
awards.bestDefense: Mike D.'s Texans scored 10, the best defensive number of the week, while Houston lost to fall to 0-3. The same unit gave him -4 in Week 1.
awards.boom: Bijan Robinson, projected 17.3, scored 34.3 for Sam.
awards.bust: De'Von Achane, projected 17.3, scored 1.7 for Brett A. and is now on injured reserve.
awards.luckiestWin: Brett A. won with the eighth-best score of the week because Foy benched the difference.
awards.toughestLoss: Jeff scored 96.9, sixth-best in the league, and ran into Sam.

commentary.outro:
Week 4's marquee game is Jordan against Foy, first against seventh, and Foy needs it more: he has the hardest remaining schedule in the league and just handed away a game he had won. Mike D. and Baker meet in a matchup of the week's top score against the week's hottest running back, Sam brings his three-defense rotation against Mark, and Hess plays Frum in a game somebody has to win.

Trade Desk: running backs are the currency this season. Sam and Baker have nobody healthy behind their two starters, and Hess, Danny and Mark are one injury from starting a back who projects under six points a game. The sellers are Mike D. (Cam Skattebo), Jeff (Tony Pollard), Jordan (Rhamondre Stevenson), Frum (Jadarian Price) and Brett A. (Aaron Jones). Skattebo to Sam is the cleanest fit on the board, and Baker has five receivers to pay for a back. Danny has receivers to spare and Frum needs one, so Matthew Golden for Price fixes both rosters. Hess needs a back and a receiver and has nothing spare to trade, which is how a 1-2 team becomes a 1-5 team. Move of the week: Sam picking up Tyler Shough on Wednesday and starting him for 23.8. Anti-move of the week: Foy picking up the Giants defense on Sunday, benching it for an Eagles unit that scored -1, and losing by 1.8.

Swish Watch: the reigning champion is 2-1 and sixth, which undersells the week-to-week ride: 104.4, then 142.4, then an 88.7 that won by less than two points. The $97 running back duo of Saquon Barkley and De'Von Achane has produced 40.6 points in three weeks, and Achane is now on injured reserve. Travis Kelce has scored 42.1 over the same stretch, one of those weeks from the bench. The Swish is safe for now, mostly because Josh Allen is. Keeper Corner opens next week, and a few of you should start drafting statements.
